profile.reading:
DartPoints operates a data center at 302 West 3rd Street, Unit 400, in downtown Cincinnati, Ohio, under the company code CVG01 referencing the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky airport designation. This facility traces its origin to Immedion, a Greenville, South Carolina-headquartered colocation provider founded in 2007 that operated eight data centers across seven markets, including two Cincinnati locations, before DartPoints announced its acquisition of the company on March 16, 2021. DartPoints subsequently renovated this downtown Cincinnati facility, with the completed remodel announced around January 2024 and independently corroborated by the Cincinnati Business Courier, a local business publication, which covered the renovated center in a February 2024 article and followed up in September 2024 on how the upgrade was fueling local business and technology expansion, though the full text of both articles was paywalled and only headlines and summaries could be confirmed this session. The current facility spans 14,715 square feet of slab floor space with a 13,200-square-foot data hall, drawing 1.6 megawatts of utility power against a 180-kilowatt critical IT load, cooled by 310 tons of capacity, and connecting through 8 on-site network providers. The specific investment amount for the 2024 remodel, and whether it corresponds to one or both of Immedion's original two Cincinnati sites, were not disclosed in any source reached this session. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no Uptime Institute Tier certification level is stated for this building.

DartPoints markets itself company-wide as serving more than 900 enterprise customers, including universities, hospital systems, and Fortune 500 companies, and has been recognized on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private US companies in multiple recent years.

reading.body:
DartPoints Cincinnati publishes 1.6 MW of IT capacity at a downtown Cincinnati address. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this represents roughly 40 racks, or if fully deployed for accelerator hosting at 10 kW per accelerator, roughly 160 units. The facility ranks eighth among eight Ohio data centers with published capacity figures, representing 2.6 percent of the state's published 60.4 MW.

DartPoints Cincinnati qualifies under SOC 2 Type II compliance for enterprise-grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure. The operator emphasizes AI-ready, high-density infrastructure and 99.999 percent uptime across its portfolio. DartPoints is now majority-controlled by NOVA Infrastructure as of April 2025, with combined committed growth capital exceeding 250 million dollars across the operator's expansion.

This campus sits in Ohio, which has 76 mapped data center facilities but only eight with published power figures. Cincinnati's 1.6 MW is too small to move the needle on state-level AI scaling or grid constraints. Its relevance is to regional enterprise customers in a Tier 2 market, not to the national AI infrastructure build.
